key_insight: SkillBrowser improves agent performance by loading only the skills needed at the right moment, instead of exposing a whole skill library or relying on one-shot retrieval.
engineering_relevance: For scalable agent systems, selective skill exposure can reduce context pollution while keeping procedural knowledge available when reasoning reveals a new capability need.
method: Uses a Meta-Skill to monitor the agent’s current capability gap.
Formulates targeted queries during reasoning, then loads only the relevant skills on demand.
Avoids static skill selection based solely on the initial task prompt.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on six SRA-Bench subsets with five LLMs, where SkillBrowser improved aggregate accuracy over static retrieval and LLM-based selection, including multi-step tool use.
watch_item: Benefits are model- and task-dependent, and the framework can incur extra latency while still under-invoking useful skills in some cases.
paper_title: SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill-Using Agents
